repo_notes.content: Write in English for firmware developers and maintainers. Start each page with what the reader can do or check, cite the evidence relevant to that topic, and link to other pages for procedures owned there.

mruby/c is the runtime compiled into the firmware. mruby supplies the host compiler mrbc. mrubyc-zephyr packages the runtime and the Zephyr HAL. Use the bundled release and pinned compiler documented in README.md and vendor/mrubyc/src/VERSION.

Use README.md and docs/ruby-guide.md for user-facing procedures and worked examples. Use zephyr/Kconfig for defaults, ranges, and dependencies and zephyr/CMakeLists.txt for compile definitions. Use vendored source for Ruby and C API behavior.

Page notes include revision-specific facts and links to repository documentation. When indexed source excerpts are incomplete, give the supplied facts with their named documentation links and keep other claims within the available evidence. Do not invent source citations or turn unrelated CI YAML into evidence for Ruby, allocation, or Kconfig behavior.

For Ruby recipes, use runnable examples from docs/ruby-guide.md or checked-in samples. Preserve prerequisites and expected output. Separate the supported mruby/c methods and tested configurations from broader Ruby or mruby behavior.
Show which steps run on the host and which run in firmware. Keep ownership explicit for the pool, the bytecode arrays, the Zephyr thread, Ruby tasks, and heap values passed to C.

Write Kconfig names with CONFIG_ in prj.conf examples. Distinguish configurable defaults from resolved values, choice members, hidden symbols, upstream defines, and read-only menu comments. All runtime options are under CONFIG_MRUBYC.
When discussing runtime compatibility or security, link README.md and SECURITY.md. Explain the trusted-bytecode boundary, application impact, and private reporting path at the advisory level.
Distinguish supported configurations, CI coverage on native_sim and qemu_cortex_m3, and physical-board validation. Use the actual test scenarios for claims about observed behavior.
Use checked-in files as the authority for pins and release policy. Examples that name a tag require that tag to exist. Give an appropriate checkout-based workflow where a tag is unavailable.

pages.title: Getting Started with mruby/c on Zephyr
pages.purpose: Choose an entry point and follow the path from a Ruby script to a working Zephyr application. Start with README.md and samples/hello/main.c.

page_notes.content: Explain the Ruby source → host mrbc → embedded C array → runtime → Zephyr HAL flow. The application provides memory for the pool and runs mrbc_init(), mrbc_create_task(), and mrbc_run() on one Zephyr thread.

Give two entry points, running the checked-in sample or adding the module to an existing application. Link to the application workflow and to Writing Ruby for Firmware for supported scripting patterns.
Use west.yml, zephyr/module.yml, and the source tree to identify the workspace, sample apps, module (CMake and Kconfig), and vendor runtime. Keep setup steps on the child pages.

pages.title: What Is mruby/c?
pages.purpose: Explain what mruby/c contributes to small embedded applications and how it relates to Ruby, mruby, and mrbc. Use README.md and the official mruby/c release4.0.0 README.
pages.parent: Getting Started with mruby/c on Zephyr

page_notes.content: Explain what the VM, built-in classes, embedded Ruby library, allocator, and scheduler each do. Cite vendor/mrubyc/src/mrubyc.h and link to Runtime and Memory Measurement for internals.
In this revision the runtime is mruby/c 4.0.0, the host compiler is mrbc 4.0.0 from mruby, and the bytecode format is RITE0400. Do not imply general Ruby or mruby library compatibility.

The official mruby/c 4.0.0 README lists RAM usage under 40 KB in its mruby comparison. Its sample_c/sample_include.c reserves a 40 KiB pool. Applications choose their own pool size. Link README.md#memory-footprint-rom-and-ram and Measure ROM and RAM for the Zephyr numbers.

pages.title: Supported Targets and Toolchains
pages.purpose: Select a Zephyr board and toolchain using west.yml, README.md, zephyr/Kconfig, and .github/workflows/ci.yml.
pages.parent: Getting Started with mruby/c on Zephyr

page_notes.content: State the 32-bit little-endian, non-SMP, multithreading and system clock requirements. Ruby's optional 64-bit Integer does not change the target CPU requirements.
Document Zephyr 3.7.2 LTS, native_sim/native with the host toolchain and 32-bit compiler support, and qemu_cortex_m3 with Zephyr SDK 0.16.9 and QEMU.
Explain the difference between the native_sim/native build qualifier and the Twister native_sim platform name. Link to the test scenarios for what each platform actually exercises.

pages.title: Run Hello and the Task Scheduling Sample
pages.purpose: Build and run the examples from samples/hello and samples/vm_tasks using the README.md west workflow.
pages.parent: Getting Started with mruby/c on Zephyr

page_notes.content: Use the samples' CMakeLists.txt, prj.conf, and sample.yaml files to show board commands, required configuration, and expected output. Use the checked-in bytecode headers so the first sample can run without host mrbc.
Describe Hello's aligned 16 KiB application pool and the two-task sample's aligned 24 KiB pool. Point out the task-creation result check before running the scheduler.
For the scheduling sample show a:start, b:ran, a:done, then the scheduler return status. Explain the ordering with task_a.rb and task_b.rb and link to Ruby Tasks, Waiting, and Timing.

pages.title: Add the Module to a Zephyr Application
pages.purpose: Show west manifest and local-checkout integration using README.md, west.yml, zephyr/module.yml, and samples/hello/main.c.
pages.parent: Getting Started with mruby/c on Zephyr

page_notes.content: Show where to place the manifest project, what west update retrieves, and how to use EXTRA_ZEPHYR_MODULES for a local checkout. Explain where a checked-out module and Zephyr will be found.

Show CONFIG_MRUBYC=y, CONFIG_PRINTK=y, and a compatible Zephyr clock using the Hello prj.conf. Link to the Kconfig reference for available options and to the embedding page for generating the app's bytecode.
Use the aligned application pool, lifetime of pool and bytecode arrays, and checked mrbc_create_task() result. Show what the application does after mrbc_run() returns.

pages.title: Compile Ruby and Embed Bytecode
pages.purpose: Generate bytecode manually or as part of a CMake build using README.md and cmake/mrubyc.cmake.
pages.parent: Getting Started with mruby/c on Zephyr

page_notes.content: Show the host mrbc version check and a manual mrbc -B command to emit a named C array. Explain --remove-lv, trusted source input, bytecode lifetime, and giving each script a unique C identifier.

Show mrubyc_embed_script(app app_mrb app.rb) after find_package(Zephyr), with CONFIG_MRUBYC=y. Explain the per-target output directory, automatic include path, and host executable discovery by PATH or absolute MRUBYC_MRBC.

Explain how the helper checks compiler version, tracks dependencies and checks the RITE prefix before publishing its output. Link to the upgrade guide for regeneration and to the loader page for runtime validation.

pages.title: Writing Ruby for Firmware
pages.purpose: Guide application developers through practical idioms and examples in docs/ruby-guide.md for the pinned mruby/c 4.0.0 and mrbc 4.0.0.

page_notes.content: Use the guide to show how to build and run a recipe with pinned mrbc and Hello. Link to the Write and port Ruby section for CRuby alternatives, failure recovery, and how to verify behavior in the resolved firmware configuration.
Prefer explicit bounds and units, predictable allocation in loops, and a specific rescue where the caller can recover. Link to the relevant recipe instead of pasting whole scripts repeatedly.

Link docs/ruby-guide.md#design-peripheral-io for application binding design using the pinned Common I/O API Guidelines. Describe GPIO, ADC, PWM, UART, I2C, and SPI as application-side contracts. The repository supplies the VM, scheduler, and Zephyr HAL.

pages.title: Integers, Floats, Strings, and Encodings
pages.purpose: Choose value types and text operations using docs/ruby-guide.md, vendor/mrubyc/src/c_numeric.c, vendor/mrubyc/src/c_string.c, and zephyr/Kconfig.

page_notes.content: Explain 32-bit default Ruby Integer, optional 64-bit Integer, Float precision choices and optional Math. State why input bounds matter before arithmetic. Link to the documented 32-bit minimum literal and mixed-type arithmetic limitations.

Show how the guide reads a two-byte big-endian field with bytesize and getbyte. Use byteslice for byte slicing. Explain that UTF-8 indexing applies to specific String methods and that Unicode case conversion depends on UTF-8 and covers the Basic Multilingual Plane.

Explain how to check the actual method table in vendor/mrubyc/src/_autogen_class_string.h and how to verify non-ASCII behavior under the intended Kconfig. Link to Language Features and Bytecode Options for defaults.

pages.title: Collections, Blocks, and Symbols
pages.purpose: Select collection operations that fit the pool budget using docs/ruby-guide.md, vendor/mrubyc/src/c_array.c, vendor/mrubyc/src/c_hash.c, and vendor/mrubyc/src/symbol.c.

page_notes.content: Show the guide's select and each example and expected 640 and 910 outputs. Explain map versus select versus each and bound the inputs when building result arrays.

Use the guide's porting table for explicit block alternatives to Symbol-to-Proc and chained enumerators. Verify methods in the generated class tables and the embedded Ruby library. Explain how to check for missing Hash keys and how to preserve false in default values.
Use a bounded set of symbol names instead of interning arbitrary strings. Explain why dynamic symbols consume capacity and how this relates to the sizing and profiling pages.

pages.title: Input Validation, Exceptions, and Recovery
pages.purpose: Use docs/ruby-guide.md, README.md#known-limitations, and tests/fatal_hooks/testcase.yaml to connect recoverable errors to the VM exception policy.

page_notes.content: Use the interval_ms recipe for input types, bounds, and a specific rescue. Describe how to distinguish nil, false, zero and empty strings when they have different meanings.

Use the guide's Ruby fake transfer for bounded polling and cleanup on completion and timeout. Link to the documented return-through-ensure limitation and distinguish the fake from any physical driver tests.

Explain that handled exceptions do not invoke the shutdown hook. A VM ending with an unhandled exception has a separate configurable policy. Link to Diagnostics, Fatal Hooks, and C API for Task.create behavior.

pages.title: Ruby Tasks, Waiting, and Timing
pages.purpose: Build predictable task workflows using docs/ruby-guide.md, samples/vm_tasks, vendor/mrubyc/src/rrt0.c, and zephyr/hal/hal.c.

page_notes.content: Explain how the two-task sample demonstrates sleep_ms and scheduler interleaving. Show the bounded three-iteration wait example from the guide, including its output and application prerequisites.

Use the scheduler source for Task methods, priorities and states, Task.pass, and the distinction between tasks loaded from C and Ruby Task.create. Explain the lifetime difference and link the latter to the exception hook.
Explain why code in a long C call occupies the owning thread, how the HAL timer drives Ruby scheduling, and how tick rounding affects waits. Link to Scheduler, Timer, and Console Options for values.

pages.title: Call C from Ruby
pages.purpose: Write a small binding using docs/ruby-guide.md, vendor/mrubyc/src/class.h, vendor/mrubyc/src/value.h, and zephyr/CMakeLists.txt.

page_notes.content: Use the check_percent recipe for registration after mrbc_init(), validation of count, type and range, and return of a value or an exception. Show the Ruby-side expected output. Keep the example independent of a physical driver.

Use poll_period and vendor/mrubyc/src/value.h for keyword presence versus nil, mandatory and unknown keyword validation, and cleanup after raising. Explain the receiver/return slot, borrowed, retained, and transferred references, and instance destructors.

Show where to link MRUBYC_API and why configuration and value layouts must agree. Link docs/ruby-guide.md#design-peripheral-io for resource ownership, buffer lifetime, timeout and cancellation, fake backend coverage, and bounded ISR notifications delivered to the owning VM thread.

pages.title: Runtime and Memory Measurement
pages.purpose: Explain the path from embedded script to allocation, execution, and measurement using samples/hello/main.c and the vendored runtime.

page_notes.content: Use a small source-linked overview of the C startup path, bytecode loading, task scheduling, and pool allocation. Point readers to the relevant child pages for API details.
Identify distinct limits to investigate when tuning the application, including pool space, runtime table capacity, configured registers, and the Zephyr thread stack.
Point to the ROM and RAM comparison and the profiling guide. Keep linker totals and runtime pool occupancy distinct.

pages.title: Bytecode Loading, Alignment, and VM Dispatch
pages.purpose: Trace RITE loading and execution using vendor/mrubyc/src/load.c, vendor/mrubyc/src/vm.c, vendor/mrubyc/src/opcode.h, and zephyr/CMakeLists.txt.

page_notes.content: Follow task creation through accepted RITE0400 bytecode, IREP construction, and VM dispatch. Explain that the version check checks format compatibility and that embedded bytecode must come from trusted sources.
Use the RITE0300 rejection in tests/mrubyc/main.c and the OP_EXT scenario in tests/mrubyc/testcase.yaml as evidence. Describe extended operands as a runtime capability tied to the build option.

Explain little-endian target selection, conditional MRBC_REQUIRE_32BIT_ALIGNMENT for ARM Baseline or CONFIG_TRAP_UNALIGNED_ACCESS, and upstream 64-bit alignment policy. Use the trap-enabled Cortex-M3 test as the specific coverage.

pages.title: Ruby Values and Reference Ownership
pages.purpose: Explain value representations and heap lifetime using vendor/mrubyc/src/value.h, vendor/mrubyc/src/boxing_no.h, and vendor/mrubyc/src/class.c.

page_notes.content: Describe tagged value types in the supported layout and which values use a reference count. Connect precision and integer width to the compile-time representations.

Trace ownership from C accessor through return slot or container storage. Explain mrbc_incref(), mrbc_decref(), and when instance destructor registration is available. Link to Call C from Ruby for the binding example.
Explain that Kconfig and the MRUBYC_API interface keep compile definitions consistent across runtime and C extensions. Link to Fixed and Unavailable Upstream Modes for unsupported layouts.

pages.title: Built-ins, Symbols, and Method Lookup
pages.purpose: Explain what is available to Ruby and how it is resolved using vendor/mrubyc/src/class.c, vendor/mrubyc/src/mrblib.c, vendor/mrubyc/src/symbol.c, and vendor/mrubyc/src/keyvalue.c.

page_notes.content: Distinguish generated built-in class and symbol tables from the bytecode in mrblib.c. Explain why C method tables and the embedded Ruby library both matter when checking which methods are present.
Trace method, constant, and instance variable lookup. Tie dynamic symbols and key-value growth to the capacity options without conflating generated symbols with MRUBYC_MAX_SYMBOLS_COUNT.
Explain the default tree and optional linear dynamic symbol search and why symbol interning and key-value growth affect a constrained pool. Link to the collections recipe and capacity table.

pages.title: Size and Profile the Memory Pool
pages.purpose: Use samples/hello/main.c, vendor/mrubyc/src/alloc.h, vendor/mrubyc/src/alloc.c, and tests/mrubyc/main.c to measure an application's allocator usage.

page_notes.content: Explain the application-owned aligned array, the upstream pool allocator, and how task and heap usage draw from it. Describe mrbc_alloc_statistics() and start, stop, and get profiling when CONFIG_MRUBYC_ALLOC_PROFILING=y.
Use the optional-features test for an example of reading initial, peak, and minimum usage. Explain why persistent allocations at the tail appear at the next ordinary allocation or release sample.

Give a repeatable process for tuning with realistic workloads: measure startup and concurrent tasks, take a representative pool peak, allow for workload variation, and check Zephyr thread stack independently. Link to the OOM statistics and footprint pages.

pages.title: Measure ROM and RAM
pages.purpose: Reproduce the qemu_cortex_m3 firmware comparison from README.md#memory-footprint-rom-and-ram and interpret what the linker's memory regions include.

page_notes.content: Report the README.md table in bytes. C Hello with CONFIG_MRUBYC=n is 7,850 FLASH and 7,168 static RAM. mruby/c Hello is 72,724 FLASH and 26,368 static RAM. The increases are 64,874 and 19,200, of which 16,384 RAM bytes are the reserved pool and 2,816 bytes are the rest of the static RAM difference.

Use qemu_cortex_m3, Zephyr 3.7.2, SDK 0.16.9 with Arm GCC 12.2.0, Picolibc, size optimization, printk, 1 kHz system clock, 4 KiB main stack, default mruby/c settings, and BUILD_VERSION=v3.7.2. Both builds printed the same two messages. Link to the exact C baseline source and build commands in the README.

Explain FLASH and RAM linker totals, the pool in .bss and included stack reservations, and how to attribute symbols with rom_report and ram_report. Link to the README's upstream under-40-KB comparison and distinguish reserved RAM from measured workload occupancy.

pages.title: Kconfig Reference
pages.purpose: Provide a complete navigation index for zephyr/Kconfig, README.md#configuration, and zephyr/CMakeLists.txt. Use the child pages for the detailed settings tables.

page_notes.content: Show CONFIG_MRUBYC (n by default). It depends on MULTITHREADING && SYS_CLOCK_EXISTS && !SMP && !BIG_ENDIAN && !64BIT. CONFIG_APP_LINK_WITH_MRUBYC_API is hidden and defaults to y under MRUBYC so the Zephyr app inherits MRUBYC_API.

Explain prj.conf versus menuconfig and how to verify resolved values in <build-dir>/zephyr/.config. Show west build -d <build-dir> -t menuconfig and state that unavailable and fixed entries are read-only comments.

Link to the four setting groups covering all 26 runtime symbols, including both members of the MRUBYC_FLOAT choice, plus the page for the 11 read-only comments. Each settings table gives exact names, defaults, dependencies or ranges, and the compile-time mapping.

pages.title: Capacity, Symbols, and Pool Profiling Options
pages.purpose: Document the seven memory and capacity controls from zephyr/Kconfig and their mappings in zephyr/CMakeLists.txt.

page_notes.content: CONFIG_MRUBYC_MAX_VM_COUNT defaults to 5 (1–255) → MAX_VM_COUNT. CONFIG_MRUBYC_MAX_REGS_SIZE defaults to 110 (32–65535) → MAX_REGS_SIZE. CONFIG_MRUBYC_MAX_SYMBOLS_COUNT defaults to 255 (32–32512) → MAX_SYMBOLS_COUNT. Explain what resource each limits.

CONFIG_MRUBYC_SYMBOL_SEARCH_LINEAR defaults to n (binary tree) → MRBC_SYMBOL_SEARCH_LINEAR when enabled. CONFIG_MRUBYC_KV_SIZE_INIT defaults to 2 (1–64) → MRBC_KV_SIZE_INIT. CONFIG_MRUBYC_KV_SIZE_INCREMENT defaults to 5 (1–64) → MRBC_KV_SIZE_INCREMENT. Explain the allocation and lookup tradeoffs.

CONFIG_MRUBYC_ALLOC_PROFILING defaults to n → MRBC_USE_ALLOC_PROF when enabled. Explain the API at a high level and link to Size and Profile the Memory Pool. The application's pool and thread stack are sized separately from these settings.

pages.title: Language Features and Bytecode Options
pages.purpose: Document the seven language and bytecode controls from zephyr/Kconfig, zephyr/CMakeLists.txt, and vendor/mrubyc/src/vm_config.h.

page_notes.content: MRUBYC_FLOAT chooses CONFIG_MRUBYC_FLOAT_SINGLE (default n, MRBC_USE_FLOAT=1) or CONFIG_MRUBYC_FLOAT_DOUBLE (default y, MRBC_USE_FLOAT=2). CONFIG_MRUBYC_USE_MATH defaults to n → MRBC_USE_MATH and requires NATIVE_LIBC, PICOLIBC, NEWLIB_LIBC, or EXTERNAL_LIBC. An external libc must provide libm.

CONFIG_MRUBYC_USE_STRING_UTF8 defaults to n → MRBC_USE_STRING_UTF8. CONFIG_MRUBYC_USE_UNICODE_CASE defaults to n → MRBC_USE_UNICODE_CASE and requires UTF-8 indexing. Give its BMP scope and link to the text examples.

CONFIG_MRUBYC_INT64 defaults to n (32-bit Integer) → MRBC_INT64 when enabled. CONFIG_MRUBYC_SUPPORT_OP_EXT defaults to y → MRBC_SUPPORT_OP_EXT when enabled. Explain the need to rerun representative app scripts after either change.

pages.title: Scheduler, Timer, and Console Options
pages.purpose: Document the six scheduler and console settings using zephyr/Kconfig, zephyr/CMakeLists.txt, zephyr/hal/hal.c, and vendor/mrubyc/src/rrt0.c.

page_notes.content: CONFIG_MRUBYC_TICK_UNIT_MS defaults to 1 (1–10 ms) → MRBC_TICK_UNIT. CONFIG_MRUBYC_TIMESLICE_TICK_COUNT defaults to 10 (1–255 ticks) → MRBC_TIMESLICE_TICK_COUNT. Explain multiplication for the time slice and whole-system-tick rounding.

CONFIG_MRUBYC_TASK_NAME_LEN defaults to 15 (1–255 bytes excluding NUL) → MRBC_TASK_NAME_LEN. CONFIG_MRUBYC_SCHEDULER_EXIT defaults to y → MRBC_SCHEDULER_EXIT and returns after tasks drain; when disabled, the owning thread stays idle. Explain why waiting or suspended tasks matter.

CONFIG_MRUBYC_NO_STDIO defaults to n → MRBC_NO_STDIO when enabled. It omits p, print, puts and printf while keeping sprintf and HAL diagnostics. CONFIG_MRUBYC_CONVERT_CRLF defaults to n → MRBC_CONVERT_CRLF when enabled, and requires !UART_CONSOLE. Explain CONFIG_PRINTK for output and why the UART backend already handles CRLF.

pages.title: Diagnostics, Fatal Hooks, and C API
pages.purpose: Document the six diagnostics and C interface controls using zephyr/Kconfig, zephyr/CMakeLists.txt, zephyr/fatal_hooks.h, and tests/fatal_hooks/testcase.yaml.

page_notes.content: CONFIG_MRUBYC_EXCEPTION_CALL_NEST_LEVEL defaults to 8 (1–64) → MRBC_EXCEPTION_CALL_NEST_LEVEL. CONFIG_MRUBYC_DEBUG_REGS defaults to n → MRBC_DEBUG_REGS when enabled. Explain recorded frames and when register diagnostics are printed.

CONFIG_MRUBYC_OOM_POOL_STATS defaults to n and requires PRINTK. It implements MRBC_OUT_OF_MEMORY() to report total, used, and free bytes before the existing panic. CONFIG_MRUBYC_PANIC_ON_UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION defaults to n. It implements MRBC_ABORT_BY_EXCEPTION(vm) to panic on an unhandled exception at VM shutdown. Explain the default policies, Ruby rescue, and why a stopping Ruby Task.create task does not invoke the hook.

CONFIG_MRUBYC_INSTANCE_DESTRUCTOR defaults to y → MRBC_INSTANCE_DESTRUCTOR and controls the registration API and class layout. CONFIG_MRUBYC_DISABLE_LEGACY_VALUE_MACROS defaults to n → MRBC_NOT_RECOMMEND_TO_USE when enabled. Show how to keep application and runtime definitions aligned with MRUBYC_API.

pages.title: Fixed and Unavailable Upstream Modes
pages.purpose: Explain all 11 read-only entries and other derived upstream settings from zephyr/Kconfig and README.md#upstream-options-with-fixed-or-derived-values.

page_notes.content: Cover MRBC_USE_FLOAT=0, MRBC_USE_STRING=0, the fixed 16-bit MRBC_STRING_SIZE_T, MRBC_INT16, and MRBC_NAN_BOXING. Use the README for each reason and the official-release conditions for exposing Float-off and String-off. String-off needs clean embedded-library startup as well as a successful link.

Cover the fixed MRBC_ALLOC_24BIT mode, unavailable MRBC_ALLOC_16BIT, MRBC_ALLOC_LIBC and MRBC_ALLOC_VMID, and unavailable MRBC_NO_TIMER. Cite the README for alignment, allocation behavior, build failures, and software tick limitations.

Cover the fixed MRBC_LITTLE_ENDIAN and unavailable MRBC_BIG_ENDIAN in the shared byte order comment. Also distinguish auto-derived read alignment and NDEBUG/MRBC_DEBUG, generated symbol and class table settings, internal allocator constants, and ways to select a timer period or symbol search without copying upstream preset macros.

pages.title: Maintain, Test, and Release
pages.purpose: Trace maintenance from an upstream or Zephyr change through source sync, test evidence, and the production approval in .github/workflows/release.yml.

page_notes.content: Point maintainers to the compiler and bytecode upgrade procedure, vendor verification, CI matrix, and the release checks. Keep version and release status tied to source and published tags.
Distinguish an upstream update, a runtime integration change, and an application configuration change. Link each to the relevant checks and what they demonstrate.
Use SECURITY.md for the trusted-input support policy and private issue-reporting path. Link to the troubleshooting page for the information needed to reproduce a non-security issue.

pages.title: Pin the Compiler and Upgrade Bytecode
pages.purpose: Use scripts/build-mrbc.sh, scripts/check-bytecode.sh, vendor/mrubyc/src/VERSION, and README.md#upgrade-from-v341 to cover compiler provenance and migration.

page_notes.content: Explain the pinned source and checksum of host mrbc and how setup-mrbc makes it available in CI. For manually generated headers, use the checked-in sample regeneration and comparison procedure.
Show v3.4.1 with mrbc 3.4.0 and RITE0300 versus v4.0.0 with mrbc 4.0.0 and RITE0400. Repin west, regenerate all headers from source and clean-build. Describe rollback with the matching compiler.
Call out the mrbc_find_method() return type change in vendor/mrubyc/src/class.h and the README's known language limitations. Link to the C binding guide and the trusted-input rule in SECURITY.md.

pages.title: Twister, Integration Tests, and POSIX Smoke
pages.purpose: Run the executable checks using README.md, the sample.yaml files, tests/mrubyc/testcase.yaml, tests/fatal_hooks/testcase.yaml, and scripts/posix-smoke.sh.

page_notes.content: Map native_sim and qemu_cortex_m3 scenarios to defaults, custom options, scheduler idle, strict alignment, OP_EXT, console and fatal hooks. Explain how Twister harnesses check expected output and intentional panics.
Show the 32-bit POSIX smoke test with the official POSIX HAL and explain what the two-task output order verifies. Keep that scope separate from the Zephyr-only test assertions.
Point to tests/mrubyc/main.c for C and VM assertions and the compiler-generated Ruby fixtures. Distinguish these tests from the upstream Ruby suite and physical-board validation.

pages.title: Vendor Provenance and Licensing
pages.purpose: Verify official runtime and HAL inputs using scripts/fetch-mrubyc.sh, scripts/check-vendor.sh, vendor/mrubyc/LICENSE, and zephyr/hal/LICENSE.

page_notes.content: Show which archive and SHA-256 the fetch script verifies and what check-vendor compares byte for byte, including the generated sources and headers, VERSION and official Zephyr HAL.

Explain how check-vendor compares the upstream source list to zephyr_library_sources, and why a new upstream file requires a deliberate integration decision. Link to the matching compiler and bytecode checks.
Identify the integration license, upstream runtime license, Unicode data license, and separate HAL license using LICENSE, vendor/mrubyc/LICENSE, vendor/mrubyc/LICENSE.unicode, and zephyr/hal/LICENSE.

pages.title: GitHub Actions and Production Releases
pages.purpose: Describe the automated checks and release gate in .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/release.yml.

page_notes.content: Map parallel simulator and QEMU jobs, archive/toolchain/compiler caches, Twister artifacts, and provenance checks. Use .github/dependabot.yml, .github/workflows/security.yml, and .github/workflows/scorecard.yml for dependency and policy automation.
Explain how the tag is matched to MRUBYC_VERSION, how the commit's presence on main is verified, and how reusable CI is run against the tagged source before the production-gated publish job.
Describe the required production reviewer and v* deployment tag policy, and how to validate a released tag and run a clean sample build from it. Verify the tag in GitHub before calling it published.

pages.title: Troubleshoot Build and Runtime Problems
pages.purpose: Diagnose module discovery, compiler mismatch, missing output, task timing, and memory pressure using README.md and docs/ruby-guide.md.

page_notes.content: Guide build failures through west list, zephyr/module.yml, platform dependencies in zephyr/Kconfig, the resolved .config, and the mrbc version and MRUBYC_MRBC path checked by cmake/mrubyc.cmake.

Guide firmware failures through the task creation result and RITE format, Zephyr PRINTK and Ruby NO_STDIO settings, CRLF behavior, tick rounding, the scheduler return policy, and the two-task sample output.

For memory trouble, check aligned pool storage and runtime statistics, register limits, and Zephyr stack use. Ask for board, module and Zephyr versions, resolved settings and compiler version. Use SECURITY.md for private vulnerability reporting.
